data.title: FRO – Third Quarter and Nine Months 2026 Results
data.description:
FRONTLINE PLC REPORTS RESULTS FOR THE THIRD QUARTER ENDED SEPTEMBER 30, 2026

Frontline plc (the “Company”, “Frontline”, “we,” “us,” or “our”), today reported unaudited results for the nine months ended September 30, 2026:

Highlights

  • Profit of $641.4 million, or $2.88 per share for the third quarter of 2026 and adjusted profit1 of $530.9 million for the third quarter of 2026, or $2.38 per share.
  • Declared a cash dividend of $2.38 per share for the third quarter of 2026.
  • Reported revenues of $921.3 million for the third quarter of 2026.
  • Achieved average daily spot time charter equivalent earnings ("TCEs")2 for VLCCs, Suezmax tankers and LR2/Aframax tankers in the third quarter of 2026 of $148,500, $102,500 and $67,800 per day, respectively.
  • Sold two VLCCs built in 2017 for a total sales price of $270.0 million. The transactions generated net cash proceeds of $179.0 million, which were returned to the shareholders through the payment of a special one-time dividend of $0.80 per share in September 2026.
  • Entered into a three-year time charter-out agreement for one Suezmax tanker, built in 2016, at a rate of $80,000 per day, which commenced in October 2026.
  • Entered into a new senior secured revolving reducing credit facility in an amount of up to $731.8 million in November 2026 to refinance the $1,286.0 million secured revolving reducing credit facility, further reducing the Company’s weighted average interest rate margin to 118 bps as of the date of this report.

Lars H. Barstad, Chief Executive Officer of Frontline Management AS, commented:

“The third quarter of 2026 was defined by the escalation in the Middle East, logistical challenges and time-consuming trading patterns. Utilization has since reached extraordinary levels, and freight rates have moved to all-time highs, with asset values following and the entire tanker complex benefiting. As we are well into the fourth quarter of the year, our bookings so far are at the highest levels we have ever recorded across all three of our segments. With the majority of our spot days already fixed, Frontline is positioned to deliver its strongest result ever, both for the fourth quarter and for the full year 2026. The nine months that have passed in 2026 is likely to change the oil trading patterns considerably in the future, making us optimistic for Frontline’s earnings capacity in the years to come.”

Inger M. Klemp, Chief Financial Officer of Frontline Management AS, added:

“From June to November 2026 we reduced our financing costs through a combination of margin reductions on existing facilities for their remaining tenors and full refinancing of selected facilities, contributing to a reduction in the Company’s weighted average interest rate margin of 60 bps from 178 bps at the end of the first quarter of 2026 to 118 bps as of the date of this report.

We believe that the refinancing of, and amendments to, our existing debt facilities have been achieved on highly attractive terms, further strengthening our liquidity position while reducing our borrowing costs and cash breakeven rates. We continue to focus on maintaining our competitive cost structure, breakeven levels and solid balance sheet to ensure that we are well positioned to generate significant cash flow and create value for our shareholders.”

data.title: Honda Unveils All-new Avancier SUV With Next-generation Hybrid System
data.description:
TOKYO (dpa-AFX) - Honda Motor Co., Ltd. (HMC, 7267.T) on Friday unveiled its all-new Avancier SUV at an online world premiere, featuring its next-generation Honda Hybrid system and a newly developed platform, amid growing global demand for hybrid vehicles.

The Japanese automaker plans to roll out the new Avancier primarily in Asian markets, including Thailand, Japan and China.

Further, the company plans to launch 15 next-generation hybrid models globally by the end of the fiscal year ending March 31, 2030, starting with the new Avancier.

The Avancier is a three-row SUV designed for comfortable long-distance journeys.

It is the first Honda hybrid model to feature the company's new H mark and next-generation hybrid technology, which aims to deliver improved fuel efficiency and driving performance.

The vehicle also features a DualPower electric all-wheel-drive system, Motion Management System, Honda S+ Shift and over-the-air software updates.

In Tokyo, the shares were trading 2.35 percent lower at ¥1,748.00.

data.title: Novartis Stock Reaction to New Targets Seems Overdone — Market Talk
data.description: The market reaction to Novartis's medium-term targets seems overdone, with sales guidance as expected and executives pointing to AI gains that look set to boost profitability, RBC Capital Markets analysts say in a research note. "The +5% mid-term sales growth was in line with our expectations, and hopes for higher were unrealistic, in our view," the analysts say. Moreover, executives at the Swiss drugmaker did a good job explaining the prospects for growth drivers such as its key approved medicines Rhapsido and Kisqali, as well as drug candidates ianalumab and abelacimab, the analysts add. Novartis also detailed how AI is set to help it reduce costs and accelerate workflows, which could allow it to hit its 2029 profitability goal early, according to RBC. Novartis shares closed 3.2% lower at 127.24 Swiss francs. (adria.calatayud@wsj.com)

data.title: India’s Market Rally Has Earnings Support, Valuations Remain Reasonable: Bharti AXA Life CIO
data.description:
Aside from near-term sentiment spillover in IT services, the broader Indian market is driven by domestic earnings rather than global tech spending, says Rahul Bhuskute

Indian equities are entering a crucial phase as foreign institutional investors (FIIs) return to the market, corporate earnings gather momentum and global capital begins reassessing its exposure to technology-heavy markets. Yet questions remain over the sustainability of the rally, India’s valuation premium over emerging markets and the possibility of volatility spilling over from a correction in US technology stocks.

In an interaction with BW Businessworld, Rahul Bhuskute, Chief Investment Officer at Bharti AXA Life Insurance, discusses whether the latest FII buying marks a structural shift in global allocations or a tactical opportunity, and why he believes earnings growth can support the market’s upward trajectory. He also identifies the sectors likely to lead earnings growth, assesses the implications of an unwinding of the AI trade and outlines how investors should position their portfolios across large-caps, mid-caps and defensive sectors over the next six months.

Edited excerpts:

FIIs have returned to Indian equities. Is this a sustained reversal in sentiment or a short-term tactical move?

The November 2026 surge in FII inflows reaching roughly Rs 1.06 lakh crore, the highest monthly net inflow in two years—reflects both a tactical global rotation and a long-overdue structural reset. Tactically, global fund managers are booking profits in crowded, richly valued US and North Asian AI semiconductor plays and reallocating capital toward underperforming emerging markets.

Structurally, however, this goes deeper than a short-term trade. With India’s weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index having compressed from nearly 20 per cent in mid-2024 to around 11 per cent by mid-2026, global portfolios became severely underweight India just as domestic corporate earnings entered a multi-year acceleration phase. That said, for this tactical bounce to translate into sustained multi-quarter allocations, two macro guardrails will be critical: stabilizing global bond yields and crude oil remaining anchored below USD 95 a barrel.

Can the recent market rally sustain itself, or are valuations and earnings growth still major concerns?

The recent rally in the Nifty 50 is anchored in a genuine earnings recovery rather than speculative multiple expansion. On valuations, the market remains remarkably grounded— the Nifty 50 trades at a trailing twelve-month (TTM) price to earnings (PE) of 20.55 times, still below its 5-year median of 21.90 times.

More importantly, corporate fundamentals are doing the heavy lifting. Q2 FY27 Nifty 50 PAT surged 27 per cent year-on-year (YoY), the fastest pace in 17 quarters, while broader Nifty 500 net profit expanded 29 per cent YoY on 23 per cent revenue growth. With Nifty projected to compound at 16 per cent annually through FY28, earnings visibility is strong enough to absorb near-term volatility and sustain the uptrend without relying on valuation froth.

Large-caps are outperforming while mid-caps and small-caps remain under pressure. Is this divergence likely to continue?

In the near term, yes large-cap outperformance is likely to hold. While mid- and small-caps led the market through the first three quarters of 2026, the current rally is being powered by FII flows that overwhelmingly target liquid large-cap index heavyweights. By contrast, broader market breadth remains vulnerable, as seen in the sharp single-day pullbacks across high-beta mid- and small-cap stocks whenever volatility flares up. Given wider valuation gaps and superior liquidity, large-caps offer a much stronger risk-reward profile right now.

Which sectors are best positioned to deliver earnings growth in the second half of FY27? Which sectors face the biggest risks?

In Q2 FY27, 17 of 22 sectors posted double-digit YoY profit growth, with BFSI, Metals, Oil & Gas, and Automobiles accounting for 77 per cent of incremental corporate earnings. For H2 FY27, BFSI, Capital Goods & Power T&D, and Cement are best positioned to sustain earnings momentum supported by healthy credit expansion, strong infrastructure order books, and improving post-monsoon demand and pricing.

Conversely, Consumer Staples (FMCG) and IT face greater volatility. FMCG is navigating a high base from GST-related pricing dynamics, while IT continues to work through client spending shifts and margin pressures triggered by AI disruption.

How vulnerable are Indian equities to a correction in US technology stocks and a possible unwinding of the AI trade?

India exhibits low direct vulnerability to a US tech correction and is positioned to be a net beneficiary of an orderly AI trade unwind. Unlike Taiwan and South Korea where MSCI Emerging Markets weights climbed to 26 per cent and 23 per cent respectively due to AI hardware concentration India has negligible exposure to AI semiconductor capex.

Aside from near-term sentiment spillover in IT services (and to a certain extent in non-ferrous metals), the broader Indian market is driven by domestic earnings rather than global tech spending. Consequently, as global funds unwind crowded AI positions, India’s deep liquidity and domestic growth profile make it a natural destination for rotating capital

What impact could crude oil price volatility have on Indian markets? Which sectors stand to gain or lose?

Crude oil volatility directly shapes India’s macro stability and corporate margins, making the recent ~16 per cent pullback in Brent from October highs near USD 110 to roughly USD 92 per barrel on rising US inventories and expected supply surpluses a significant tailwind. Since India imports over 80 per cent of its oil, every USD 10/barrel decline trims the Current Account Deficit (CAD) by 0.4 per cent–0.5 per cent of GDP and cools imported inflation.

Sectorally, softer crude below USD 95/barrel boosts Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) through stronger marketing margins, while lowering input and fuel costs for downstream plays like paints, specialty chemicals, adhesives, tyres, and aviation. Conversely, upstream explorers like ONGC and Oil India face weaker realizations and any renewed geopolitical flare-up above USD 100/barrel would swiftly turn this tailwind into a broad margin and inflation headwind.

Are Indian equities attractively valued compared with other emerging markets, or should investors remain cautious at current levels?

India still trades at a premium to broader emerging markets, but a year of time-correction alongside robust earnings growth has cooled that gap from post-pandemic highs, leaving a much healthier risk-reward setup. Headline multiples also miss crucial structural differences— Taiwan (17 to 18 times forward earnings) and South Korea (10 to11 times) are dominated by cyclical semiconductor and hardware exporters, while China (10 to 11 times) faces persistent property and deflationary headwinds.

India’s market, by contrast, is driven by domestic consumption, financialization, and infrastructure sectors with far greater earnings stability that naturally command higher multiples. Rather than broad caution, current levels call for disciplined, quality-focused allocation.

Where should investors focus over the next six months: large-caps, mid-caps, small-caps or defensive sectors?

For the next six months, investors are best served by a balanced allocation anchored in quality large-caps (60 per cent–65 per cent), paired with selective growth-oriented mid-caps (20 per cent–25 per cent) and defensive healthcare/pharma (15 per cent). Even as earnings upgrades broaden across banks, industrials, and healthcare, large-caps offer the most compelling risk-reward profile trading below their 5-year and 10-year median P/E multiples while capturing 27 per cent YoY Q2 PAT growth and the bulk of returning FII liquidity.

Mid-caps, trading near fair historical multiples (27.67 times PE), offer targeted plays on domestic capex and niche financials, whereas broad small-caps carry elevated drawdown risk at an 18 per cent valuation premium. Finally, a 15 per cent allocation to domestic pharma and healthcare acts as an effective hedge against West Asian geopolitical risks and crude volatility without compromising growth.

data.title: Thyssenkrupp Automotive Appoints Chitrupa Kapoor As India HR Head
data.description:
Kapoor brings over eight years of experience at Bitwise, with expertise in people strategy, workforce planning and organisational development

Thyssenkrupp Automotive, Bilstein Motion Solutions, has appointed Chitrupa Kapoor as Head of People & Culture – India. She will lead the people and culture function in India, bringing experience across strategic HR business partnering, workforce planning, organisational development and leadership development.

Kapoor joins the automotive business after spending more than eight years at Bitwise, where she served as Senior Human Resources Business Partner. During her tenure, she led the People & Culture strategy across the company's India headquarters and US delivery units, partnering with CXOs across more than 16 business units.

Her responsibilities included workforce planning, organisational development, succession planning, employee retention and global employee experience programmes. She also worked on strengthening leadership capabilities and aligning people strategies with business requirements.

Before Bitwise, Kapoor was associated with Tata Consultancy Services as a Learning and Development Specialist, where she contributed to employee training and development initiatives.

Her earlier professional experience includes working as a Behavioural Coach and serving as HR Executive & Corporate Training Lead at Symbiosis. These roles gave her exposure to human resources, behavioural development, corporate training and employee capability building.

In her new role, Kapoor will bring together her experience in HR business partnering, talent development and organisational effectiveness to support the company's workforce and business priorities in India.

Bilstein Motion Solutions is part of thyssenkrupp Automotive Technology, the automotive business of German industrial group thyssenkrupp. Its operations span steering, suspension and chassis-related technologies for the global automotive industry.

data.title: Evonik CEO Says BASF Ending Takeover Pursuit Removes Source of Uncertainty
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud

Evonik Industries' interim Chief Executive Officer Claus Rettig said BASF's decision to abandon efforts to take over the German chemicals company removes a source of uncertainty for its employees.

"Our plan for the coming years is set. Now we can focus our full energy on Evonik's standalone development," Rettig said. "For our employees, this removes a source of uncertainty."

BASF said Thursday that it would end its pursuit of Evonik after two all-cash offers were rebuffed.

"We are convinced that BASF's derisked all-cash offer of 24 euros per share would have represented significant additional value for Evonik shareholders," BASF Chief Executive  Markus Kamieth said.

The bid valued Evonik at 11.18 billion euros ($12.26 billion), based on share-count data provided by FactSet.

Write to Adria Calatayud at adria.calatayud@wsj.com

data.title: India's eastern coast hit by third cyclone within a month
data.description:
Key points:
  • Cyclone brings heavy rain, strong winds
  • Hundreds of thousands evacuated along India's eastern coast
  • Visuals show high waves, waterlogging in some places
  • No damage reported, officials from impacted states say
  • Cyclone expected to weaken into a 'depression' by evening

Heavy rain battered India's eastern coast on Friday as Cyclone Akvan, the third such storm to hit the country in less than a month, made landfall, the weather department said.

Odisha and Andhra Pradesh states evacuated hundreds of thousands of people from vulnerable regions this week in anticipation of the cyclone, which weakened overnight to a 'cyclonic storm'.

It crossed the coast with a wind speed of 70-80 kph (44-40 mph) and gusts upto 90 kph (56 mph), the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in a statement.

Visuals showed high waves crashing against the shore and trees swaying violently with the wind, while motorcycles navigated waterlogged roads in some places amid intense rain.

"No damage or untoward incident has been reported so far," Odisha's Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh Prabhakar Patil told Reuters.

Andhra Pradesh also saw "minimal impact", disaster management official Prakhar Jain said.

IMD said the storm was expected to gradually weaken into a deep-depression over the next three hours and further into a depression in the subsequent six hours.

The cyclone comes a fortnight after severe cyclonic storm Murasu similarly struck the eastern coast, triggering the evacuation of thousands of people and uprooting some trees and electric poles.

Another cyclone, Arnab, struck the coast last month, killing six people and disrupting power supply in several places.

All three cyclones were formed over the Bay of Bengal, a major region for tropical cyclones.

The pattern of three cyclones forming within a month bears similarities to 1987, when multiple cyclonic storms struck the Bay of Bengal in quick succession after the monsoon, which is typical of El Niño years, a government weather expert told Reuters on Thursday.

data.title: Vallourec's core profit falls 26%, hit by Iran war and disruption in the US
data.description:
French steel tubes maker Vallourec reported a 25.8% fall in its third-quarter core profit on Wednesday, within its own guidance range, impacted by the Middle East crisis and a temporary operational disruption in the US.

Its earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization fell to €181 million ($199 million) in the period, compared with the €170 million to €210 million estimate it had given alongside its second-quarter results.

($1 = 0.9108 euros)

data.title: Vallourec Third Quarter 2026 Results
data.description:
Meudon (France), November 20(th) , 2026

Vallourec, a world leader in premium seamless tubular solutions, announces today its results for the third quarter 2026. The Board of Directors of Vallourec SA, meeting on November 19(th) 2026, approved the Group's third quarter 2026 Consolidated Financial Statements.

Third Quarter 2026 Results

  • Q3 Group EBITDA of $181 million within guidance, 18.9% margin
  • Tube volumes up 12% sequentially despite ongoing Middle East challenges
  • US pricing continues to strengthen, with asset utilization remaining high
  • Significant congestion at Middle East ports south of the Strait of Hormuz delaying deliveries despite resilient drilling activity
  • Challenging iron ore market conditions impacting Mine sales volumes and margins
  • EUR2.05 per share extraordinary interim dividend paid on August 5tha
  • New EUR750 million RCF arranged to align with Investment Grade profile
  • Q4 2026 Group EBITDA expected to range between $170 million and $210 million

HIGHLIGHTS & OUTLOOK

Third Quarter 2026 Results

  • Group EBITDA of US$181 million, down 26% year over year, with an EBITDA margin of 18.9%
    -- Tubes EBITDA per tonne of $592, down 18% quarter over quarter,
    reflecting less favorable price/mix effects and higher costs, particularly for Middle East logistics to be largely reimbursed in the coming quarters; and a temporary operational issue in the US relating to a subcontractor.
    -- Mine & Forest EBITDA of $30 million, down 27% year over year,
    reflecting lower iron ore market prices and sales volumes, with demand negatively impacted by elevated sea freight rates to China
  • Adjusted free cash flow of $79 million; total cash generation before warrant proceeds of $8 million, after $50m of cash outflows from other cash items, including 2026 HKM divestment payments
  • Ended the period with net debt of $100 million after $349m of warrant proceeds and $632 million in shareholder returns during the quarter

Fourth Quarter 2026 Group EBITDA is expected to range between $170 million and $210 million

  • In Tubes, volumes and EBITDA per tonne broadly in line with Q3 2026, reflecting a similar mix, additional costs related to Middle East shipments and the impact of the temporary operational issue in the US. This outlook assumes no further deterioration in waiting time for berthing at Middle East ports south of the Strait of Hormuz and no major deterioration in the region's geopolitical situation
  • In Mine & Forest, production sold is expected to be around 1.1 million tonnes

Full Year 2026 Outlook:

  • Full Year Group EBITDA is expected to range between $760 and $800 million
  • In Mine & Forest, production sold is expected to be slightly below 5.0 million tonnes for the full year

Philippe Guillemot, Chairman of the Board of Directors and Chief Executive Officer, declared:

"Vallourec delivered a resilient third quarter, with tubes volumes and revenues increasing sequentially. Profitability was impacted by additional costs in the Middle East to be largely reimbursed over the coming quarters, a less favorable mix and a challenging market environment in Mine & Forest. A temporary operational issue relating to a subcontractor contributed to lower-than-expected sequential improvement in our US business in the third quarter. After distributing an interim extraordinary dividend of EUR2.05 per share, the highest payout to shareholders in the company's history, and warrant conversion, we ended the quarter with a net debt position of $100m, well within our leverage policy.

"In the Middle East, while crude exports have increased and drilling activity has partially recovered, maritime security deteriorated late in the third quarter and into the fourth quarter, creating logistical disruptions and higher costs that led to delays in our planned deliveries and invoicing. With tube inventories in the region largely depleted, the need to prioritize tube shipments to maintain drilling operations and ensure adequate stocks is becoming critical.

"For the remainder of the year, renewed escalation in the Middle East has clouded visibility and heightened near-term shipment risks. The temporary operational issue in our US business is also expected to constrain the sequential improvement we had anticipated in the fourth quarter. Nevertheless, we expect EBITDA in the fourth quarter to be similar to the third quarter.

"Outside the Middle East, we see clear signs of improving demand, with a broad-based increase in drilling activity observable across international basins which we expect to gradually increase through 2027 on the back of a growing number of upstream project approvals. Over the quarter, we announced further major offshore awards in our longer-cycle Project Line Pipe business in Brazil, Angola and Azerbaijan, providing higher visibility on activity through 2027.

"In the United States, the market is in excellent health. Demand is firm and rising, inventories are low and falling, and seamless import volumes remain suppressed thanks to several favorable determinations by the Department of Commerce in support of fair trade. Market pricing has risen for nine consecutive months, and our customer conversations point to continued activity growth, both in oil and gas and geothermal.

"Therefore, despite the near-term challenges, we are confident in the Group's trajectory and our ability to deliver profitable growth through 2027 and beyond."

data.title: Norcod begins production at Snyen
data.description:
Norcod has welcomed its first fish to their new farm site, Snyen, in Northern Norway, bringing the cod farmer’s number of operational farming sites to seven, with an eighth site scheduled to begin operations in 2027.

“After years of administrative work and months of preparation, it is incredibly rewarding to finally release the first juveniles into the sea pens. Seeing the site come to life is a major milestone for everyone involved,” says Arve Olav Lervåg, COO of Norwegian cod farmer Norcod.

The Snyen site is ideally located in the cold waters of Meløy in Nordland, not far from one of Norcod’s other sites, Frosvika. It has maximum allowed biomass (MAB) of 3,600 tonnes, divided across 10 net pens. The site also has a concrete feed barge delivered by ScaleAQ, as well as a brand new work boat, providing the dedicated on-site team with a modern and efficient workplace.

The first stocking took place this week, with more scheduled over the coming weeks to support Norcod’s growth plans towards 25,000MT harvest by 2029. Preparations for a second approved farm location, Selsøy in the Nesna municipality, is already underway, with fish stocking estimated to commence early 2027.

Growth on track

“We are on track for our growth plans, supported by strong biological results and operations progressing as planned. Our approach has always been to build stone by stone, scaling gradually while ensuring we have the right operational and biological conditions in place. We are now starting to see the results of this approach,” says Christian Riber, CEO of Norcod.

Norcod recently published its first positive results, showing an operating profit of 23MNOK in the third quarter of 2026.

About Us

Norcod's core business is commercial sea farming of cod and is involved in the entire value chain through ownership and partnerships. Norcod’s existing fish farms are located in Mid-Norway and along the Helgeland coast with ideal conditions for cod. The company is contributing to blue ocean value creation with minimal impact on the environment while supporting local communities. Norcod is listed on Oslo’s Euronext Growth market.

data.title: Indian space startup SatSure raises $7 million from sovereign space fund
data.description:
Indian space startup SatSure has raised 600 million rupees ($7 million) from a government-backed space technology fund as part of an ongoing 2 billion rupees funding round, the company said on Friday.

The investment comes as India seeks to expand its commercial space industry through reforms that have opened the traditionally state-dominated sector to private companies and investors.

The Antariksh Venture Capital Fund is investing at a post-money valuation of 8.7 billion rupees ($93 million), SatSure said. The 16 billion rupee fund is anchored by IN-SPACe, India's private space sector regulator, and managed by SIDBI Venture Capital, an arm of state-owned small-business lender SIDBI.

Bengaluru-based SatSure uses satellite imagery and artificial intelligence to help banks, insurers, infrastructure firms and government agencies make decisions. Its subsidiary KaleidEO develops satellite imaging systems for Earth observation.

The series B round comprises 1.65 billion rupees in fresh equity, 250 million rupees in venture debt and 100 million rupees in secondary transactions. The company expects to close the round by December 2026.

The proceeds will help prepare its satellite imaging payloads for launch in 2027, support its participation in India's planned Earth-observation satellite network and expand its data analysis capabilities and international operations.

SatSure's customers include HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, ITC, Bayer and the Airports Authority of India.

The startup has raised 4.27 billion rupees from institutional investors, excluding grants, with previous backers including Baring Private Equity Partners India, Promus Ventures and Asian Development Bank Ventures.

($1 = 93.2900 Indian rupees)

data.title: Fermi shareholder Toby Neugebauer to appeal dismissal of challenge to 70% bylaw
data.description:
Toby Neugebauer, Fermi Inc.’s co-founder and largest shareholder, said Nov. 19 that he plans to appeal a Texas Business Court ruling dismissing his claims against the company. Shares of the data center real estate investment company closed down 16% on Thursday.

The lawsuit challenged a bylaw amendment adopted by Fermi’s board in May that requires shareholders to approve certain changes with 70% of all outstanding shares.

The amendment requires that threshold to expand the board or change the process for amending the bylaws. The board can make changes to those rules with a simple majority vote of directors, according to Neugebauer’s statement.

He said the amendment was adopted during a shareholder contest and without a shareholder vote. Fermi’s board also changed director elections in August to require the support of a majority of all outstanding shares, with unvoted shares counted as votes against.

At the company’s Oct. 30 annual meeting, neither of the two directors on the ballot reached that threshold. Both remain on the board, the release said. “Directors who could not win a majority of the shareholder support are still sitting in the boardroom,” Neugebauer said.

He said the court’s ruling gives shareholders a higher threshold to change the bylaws than the board faces when changing them, and said he disagrees with the decision and intends to appeal.

data.title: LEPAS L8, L6 and L4 Earn Five-Star Ratings in 2026 Euro NCAP Assessment
data.description:
WUHU, China, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- LEPAS, Chery Auto’s Premium NEV brand, has secured five-star safety ratings for its L8, L6 and L4 models under the 2026 assessment protocols. The ratings were announced by the European New Car Assessment Programme (Euro NCAP) on November 18, 2026, as part of its latest assessment covering 10 models across four key areas: Safe Driving, Crash Avoidance, Crash Protection and Post Crash Safety.

The 2026 protocols mark Euro NCAP's most significant update since 2009, introducing more demanding assessments across four areas of vehicle safety. The revised tests place greater emphasis on real-world scenarios, including complex junctions, cyclist dooring and post-crash rescue. In this round, the LEPAS L4 scored 84% in Crash Avoidance, while both the L6 and L8 achieved 87% in Crash Protection and 95% in Post Crash Safety.

The three five-star ratings highlight Chery Auto's extensive experience in vehicle safety development and validation, backed by more than 1,500 crash tests annually across over 67 scenarios. Leveraging Chery Group's "1+7+N" global R&D network, LEPAS brings this expertise to the intelligent LEX Platform. The platform integrates multiple layers of protection covering vehicle structure, occupant safety, battery safety and emergency response, complemented by redundant active safety systems and 360-degree battery protection.

LEPAS is Chery Auto's Premium NEV brand, dedicated to creating elegant mobility experiences for users worldwide. Committed to becoming the Preferred Brand for Elegant Mobility Life, LEPAS brings together Leopard Aesthetics, Elegant Technology, and Exquisite Space - transforming elegance into a driving experience you can see, feel, and trust. Supported by a growing global dealer network of more than 500 sales and service outlets, LEPAS is expanding its international footprint through localized operations, delivering products and experiences tailored to users across global markets.

data.title: Anthropic’s $81B IPO draws half the net retail buying of SpaceX’s
data.description:
Retail investors traded $772 million in Anthropic shares on its Nasdaq debut Thursday, but their net purchases totaled just $60 million, about half the $118 million they put into SpaceX on its first day of trading in June.

Anthropic’s first-day retail trading volume topped SpaceX’s $669 million and was the highest for any market debut in Vanda Research’s data, which go back to 2012, Yahoo Finance reported.

Volume counts both purchases and sales, while net buying measures how much purchases exceeded sales.

The Claude AI developer and its existing shareholders offered 980 million shares at $83 each in the $81.34 billion initial public offering (IPO). Anthropic shares opened on Nasdaq at $111.50 on Thursday, 34.3% above the IPO price, and closed at $97.17 for a first-day gain of 17.1%.

SpaceX shares gained 19.2% in their June 12 debut, closing at $160.95 against an IPO price of $135, according to Nasdaq. Although Anthropic’s base offering exceeded SpaceX’s initial $75 billion sale, SpaceX ultimately raised $85.7 billion after underwriters exercised their option to purchase additional shares.

Before the IPO, Vanda forecast about $250 million in net retail buying, more than four times Thursday’s total. Its forecast drew on retail trading in past market debuts and the volume of Anthropic perpetual futures traded on decentralized exchange Hyperliquid.

Shortly before Nasdaq trading began, those futures traded at $110.48, just 0.9% below the stock’s opening price.

data.title: Accumulate Physicswallah; target of Rs 144: Prabhudas Lilladher
data.description:
Prabhudas Lilladher's research report on Physicswallah

We attended PWL IN’s investor day wherein management highlighted plans to achieve revenues of ~INR90-100bn with a pre-IND AS EBITDA margin of 20%+ by FY30E. We believe growth vectors are in place as PWL IN intends to expand presence into prepre-foundation (~60mn TAM), boards (~57mn TAM), vernacular, and skilling (~91mn TAM). Deepening presence into South (under 5% penetration currently) and premiumization should further aid growth. Consequently, we expect sales CAGR of 24% over FY26-FY30E (implied sales CAGR of 23%/27% at lower/higher end of the management guidance over FY26-FY30E). Further, as growth investments (NEET PG, skills, Curious Jr and vernacular) mature and offline business migrates towards path to profitability (pre-IND AS EBITDA breakeven expected in FY27E), we expect pre-IND AS EBITDA CAGR of 60% over FY26-FY30E.

Outlook

The stock trades at 39x/24x over our preInd AS EBITDA (adjusting for ESOP cost) estimate for FY28E/FY29E. Retain ACCUMULATE with a SoTP based TP of INR144 (online/offline business valued at 35x/15x Sep-28E pre-IND AS EBITDA; no change in target multiple).

data.title: South African rand near one-year low with coalition talks in focus
data.description:
The South African rand touched a one-year low in early trade on Friday, weakening on uncertainty over coalition talks after local elections, compounded by pressure from a stronger dollar and a hawkish split in a central bank decision to hold rates.

  • By 0540 GMT, the rand traded at 17.56 against the dollar , hovering near its weakest in 12 months

  • The risk-sensitive currency has recently been pressured by a firmer greenback, which has flirted with a 19-month high, and uncertainty around the coalition talks, while a hawkish split in the central bank's decision to hold rates underscored persistent inflation concerns

  • Thursday's decision was a close call, with four Monetary Policy Committee members voting to keep the policy rate unchanged and three favouring a 25-basis-point increase

  • Investors are focusing on coalition talks as a key test of whether increasingly fragmented politics can deliver stable governance in South Africa's economic hub

  • As the African National Congress and its partners negotiate local power-sharing, it is nearing a deal with smaller rivals to govern Johannesburg, sidelining the pro-business Democratic Alliance despite its first-place finish in the city

  • "Ousting the DA at the local government level could spill over into the GNU, potentially destabilising national politics and having more significant implications for investor sentiment," the Bureau for Economic Research said in a weekly review note

  • South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond (ZAR2035=) was steady in early deals, with the yield at 8.635%

ARB Info

Arbitrum is a layer 2 scaling solution designed for the Ethereum network. Its goal is to increase the scalability of Ethereum while preserving its decentralization and security.

Arbitrum operates by batching many transactions together off-chain and then submitting a single, combined proof of all these transactions to the Ethereum base layer. This greatly reduces the amount of computation and storage that the Ethereum network has to handle, allowing it to support a much higher throughput of transactions.
